model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: Manager's management fees paid/payable in units, FY25/26 distribution statement (N2IU.SI_Annual_FY2026.txt:268-269): S$17.931m. Added back in distributable income as non-cash; deducted here as the REIT analogue of SBC because it is paid in new units.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T09:06:01Z (SGX regular session close, Yahoo chart API; meta.currency=SGD)
inputs.share_count_basis: Units in issue and to be issued at 31 Mar 2026 (5,284,370k; N2IU.SI_Annual_FY2026.txt:542). Held flat: the units issued for manager fees are charged as an expense in the flows (sbc_pct_path), so growing the count too would double-count.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: Owner AFFO FY26 = amount available for distribution to Unitholders 421.38 - manager fees paid in units 17.93 - maintenance capex at 4.5% of revenue 39.03 = 364.42. Distributable income is already after finance costs, tax and perpetual-securities distributions, so it is capitalised at the cost of equity with net debt held at zero.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in SGD (flows are SGD-reported; overseas HK/China/Japan/Korea income is translated and largely hedged). SGS 10y ~2.3% + ERP 5.0% x beta ~0.9 + ~0.2% for the North Asia exposure (HK Festival Walk, Beijing/Shanghai offices) = ~7.0% base. Bull 6.5%, bear 7.75%. This is a cost of equity, not a WACC, because the stream is post-interest.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lessor; lease liabilities are immaterial (nil at 31 Mar 2026). No lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Stream is the amount distributable to Unitholders only (excludes NCI S$11.2m equity and perpetual-securities distributions S$4.4m), so no NCI or perp deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO (distributable income) capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine with net_debt = 0. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'REIT / property trust (IAS 40 fair-value, external manager)'. MPACT is an externally managed (Mapletree) S-REIT; net income is dominated by fair-value moves (FY26 -S$114.8m IP revaluation, Q4 FY26 a net loss) so P/E and owner-FCF/WACC are meaningless. Engine mapping: revenue = gross revenue; 'ebitda_margin_path' = distributable income to Unitholders as % of gross revenue (FY26 48.6%); 'sbc_pct_path' = management fees paid in units % of revenue (2.07% FY26); 'capex_pct_path' = maintenance capex % of revenue (FY26 additions to investment properties S$86.6m include AEI; FY25 S$56.7m); D&A, cash tax and working capital zero because DI is already post-tax and post-working-capital. Distribution policy: at least 90% of taxable income; payout ~100% of DI in practice. FY26 DI includes S$27.3m capital distribution (FY25 S$49.9m) -- partly return-of-capital repatriation from overseas, treated as recurring in base, cut in bear. FY27 is the first full year without Mapletree Anson (divested Jul 2024), TSI/ASY (Aug 2025) and Festival Walk Tower office (Feb 2026); proceeds repaid debt (gearing 36.5%, ICR 3.2x at 31 Mar 2026). No Q1/H1 FY27 filing has been extracted; the last data point is FY26 (Mar 2026). Cross-check: NAV/unit S$1.73 at 31 Mar 2026; price/NAV ~0.68. Qualitative Analysis.json did not exist at build time; business context taken from the FY26 results announcement.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Aggregate revenue, equity and FCF 5yr CAGRs (12.6% / 9.9% / 8.1%) are inflated by the Aug-2022 MCT-MNACT merger, which was paid for in new units (units 3,323m -> 5,239m). Per-unit series are the honest growth measure: DPU -3.4% 5yr, NAV/unit +0.1% 5yr. EPS CAGRs are revaluation noise.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are owner basis (OCF - capex - manager fees in units - finance income). Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are almost identical: fees-in-units have been a stable ~2% of revenue. FY2021 base year is the COVID trough (DPU 9.49c incl. released retentions).

base.growth_rates_rationale: Y1 -4.5%: Q4 FY26 revenue run-rate S$210.7m still carried two months of Festival Walk Tower; FY27 is ~S$825-830m. Then Singapore (66% of NPI: VivoCity, MBC, mTower) positive reversions and step-ups offset by flat-to-negative overseas reversions (HK, China, Japan), ~2%.
base.ebitda_margin_path_rationale: DI/revenue 48.6% FY26; Y1 48.3% as divestment interest savings only partly offset lost NPI and capital distribution normalises; modest lift as SGD/HKD debt reprices lower and gearing stays ~36-37%.
base.terminal_cap_multiple_rationale: Cap set near the scenario's own Gordon multiple (7.0%/1.5% -> ~18.5x AFFO) so it only brakes runaway; a 15x cap would imply a terminal CoE ~8.3%, inconsistent with the discount rate. Bull 21x (6.5%/2.0% Gordon ~22.7x), bear 15x (7.75%/1.0% Gordon ~15.0x).

scenario_narratives.base: Post-divestment MPACT is a Singapore-anchored trust (61% of AUM, 66% of NPI) with a shrinking North Asia tail. FY27 DI to unitholders ~S$400m (DPU ~7.5-7.6c) after the full-year loss of Festival Walk Tower, TSI and ASY, partly offset by interest savings. Thereafter ~2% revenue growth from VivoCity and MBC reversions against soft HK/China/Japan offices, slight DI margin lift as debt costs ease. Capitalised at 7.0% CoE, 1.5% terminal growth.
scenario_narratives.bull: Singapore reversions stay high-single-digit, HK Festival Walk retail stabilises, further overseas divestments at or near book are recycled into debt reduction or Singapore assets, and SGD rates stay low. DI margin rises to ~51%; 6.5% CoE as the market re-rates a cleaner Singapore REIT toward NAV.
scenario_narratives.bear: Greater China and Japan office vacancies and negative reversions persist, HK retail weakens further, the capital-distribution component of DI falls away and renewed inflation lifts refinancing costs. Revenue falls 6% then 1% before low growth; DI margin ~46.5%, maintenance/AEI capex 5.5% of revenue, CoE 7.75%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25. Balance sheet risk is low (gearing 36.5%, ICR 3.2x, Mapletree sponsor), so no extra bear weight for solvency; but overseas office exposure and DPU that has declined three years running argue against tilting toward the bull.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the distribution stream unitholders actually receive, net of the units issued to the manager and of the capex needed to keep the buildings lettable, capitalised at an SGD cost of equity. Distributable income is post-interest, so borrowings are not deducted again. NAV (S$1.73) is a cross-check, not the valuation: external-manager REITs with declining DPU rarely trade at book.
key_risks_to_valuation: Interest-rate path: SGD/HKD refinancing costs drive the DI margin and the cost of equity simultaneously
Greater China (Festival Walk retail, Gateway Plaza, Sandhill Plaza) and Japan office occupancy and negative reversions
Capital distribution (S$27.3m FY26) may not recur at that level
External-manager fee leakage and unit issuance for fees
FX translation of HKD/JPY/RMB/KRW income against SGD
Further divestments below book would crystallise NAV losses
